purpose: Replace regex-based HTML scanning with WP_HTML_Tag_Processor/WP_HTML_Processor for reliable element identification in add_delay_load_img(), and extend maybe_serve_next_gen_images() to process <picture> <source> and <video poster> attributes.
riskRationale: A critical bug causes <picture> block optimizations (source type/srcset/sizes) to be silently dropped when non-native lazy loading is enabled, which is the most common configuration. This is a functional regression from the original regex-based approach. Additionally, the processor-based picture block extraction re-parses the full buffer on each iteration, creating a significant performance concern.
breakingChanges: <picture> block <source> type/srcset/sizes optimizations are silently dropped when non-native lazy loading mode is active (default configuration)

text: This PR makes a well-intentioned architectural improvement by adopting WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for HTML parsing, but introduces a critical regression where <picture> blocks are silently skipped when the main TagProcessor loop has already moved src→data-src on inner images. The processor-based picture extraction also re-parses the full buffer O(n) times, a significant performance concern. The maybe_serve_next_gen_images() additions for SOURCE and VIDEO tags are sound and well-implemented.

reasoning: Critical bug: picture blocks are silently skipped on WP 6.2+ when non-native lazy loading is active (the default). Important performance concern: full buffer is re-parsed up to 100 times in process_picture_blocks_processor. Both must be addressed before merge.

message: The maybe_serve_next_gen_images() extension to handle SOURCE tags (srcset) and VIDEO tags (poster) is cleanly integrated. The conditional if/elseif structure correctly dispatches between IMG/SOURCE/VIDEO without duplicating srcset parsing logic.

The data-srcset/data-sizes dual-attribute handling in process_picture_tag (?? operators on line 1501-1502) correctly accounts for both pre-processed (lazy-loaded) and raw tags inside blocks. This demonstrates good defensive design.

The two-pass WP_HTML_Processor approach in process_picture_tag (first pass collects IMG attributes, second pass applies to SOURCE tags) correctly handles the depth-based traversal to avoid escaping the <picture> scope.

The regex preg_match on line 273 looks for src="..." on the inside a block, but the main WP_HTML_Tag_Processor loop (lines 1735-1736) has already moved src to data-src for non-native lazy-loaded images. This causes the entire picture block extraction to silently fail — no type/srcset/sizes optimizations are applied. This is a functional regression from the original single-pass regex approach, which captured the original src before any modifications. The same issue exists in process_picture_blocks_regex at line 308, which is called as fallback on WP 6.2-6.4.
suggestion: Modify the regex in both process_picture_blocks_processor and process_picture_blocks_regex to match (?:data-)?src instead of just src, and adjust the capturing group index from [2] to [1]. This ensures the image URL is extracted regardless of whether the main loop has already processed it.

message: process_picture_blocks_processor creates a new WP_HTML_Processor from the full buffer on each iteration of the while loop (up to 100 iterations). Each iteration also serializes the full buffer via get_updated_html(). For a buffer with N picture blocks, this does N full HTML parses + N full serializations + N regex searches + N str_replace operations on the entire buffer. The original regex approach processed all picture blocks in a single O(buffer) preg_replace_callback pass.
suggestion: Restructure process_picture_blocks_processor to process all picture blocks in a single pass. Either: (a) use a single WP_HTML_Processor walk to find all PICTURE tags, mark them with unique markers, then iterate the marked blocks; or (b) extract all picture blocks via a single regex, then use WP_HTML_Processor only for the inner / attribute manipulation within each extracted block. The current re-parse-on-each-iteration pattern should be avoided.

message: The $found variable is set to true unconditionally before the regex extraction attempt on line 267. If preg_match fails to match the extracted picture block (e.g., marker attribute insertion corrupts the HTML), the loop continues without modifying the buffer. The same picture is found again on the next iteration, and the processor wastes up to 99 iterations doing identical failed work.
suggestion: Set $found = false before line 261 and only set it to true after a successful extraction + replacement on line 280. Add a $buffer_was_modified check to break if no progress is made.

message: str_replace($full_picture, $processed, $buffer) replaces ALL occurrences of the matched picture block in the buffer, not just the first one. If two picture blocks have identical inner HTML (e.g., the same responsive image used twice), both would be replaced with the same processed version in a single iteration. While unlikely to cause visible issues (same image = same result), the behavior is imprecise.
suggestion: Use preg_replace with a limit of 1 to ensure only the first (currently-marked) occurrence is replaced.

message: The closure in process_picture_blocks_regex uses &$img_counter and &$exclude_imgs by reference, but the function receives these as value parameters (copy of caller's variables). Changes inside the closure therefore don't propagate to the caller. This is inconsistent with process_picture_blocks_processor (which doesn't attempt to propagate changes either). While functionally harmless (picture blocks are processed after the main loop has already handled exclusions), this is confusing and should be made consistent.
suggestion: Either remove the & references from the closure's use statement to make it clear the caller is not updated, or change the function signature to accept these by reference if propagation is intended.

message: post_process_svg_placeholders uses regex to re-parse the buffer after the WP_HTML_Tag_Processor pass. Since this is a post-processing step on serialized output, regex is acceptable here. However, the placeholder '...' in the docblock description should be more descriptive.
suggestion: Update the docblock description for clarity.
